name: Manage end of term
summary: When a lease nears its end the customer must buy the equipment, renew the lease or give it back, and the lessor must collect the residual or get the equipment returned in good order. Lease administration screens the monthly maturity list, sends notices, has asset management value fair market value contracts, handles price negotiations, renewals and return instructions, rolls silent customers into month-to-month billing and asks the title team to transfer ownership once the contract is paid in full. Most contracts in a Canadian small-ticket book have a nominal or fixed purchase option and close with little work after a long calendar wait; fair market value contracts, unpaid options and customers who do not reply create most of the effort and delay.

baseline.org_archetype: A mid-size Canadian independent equipment lessor with about 55,000 active small and mid-ticket contracts on a commercial lease management system and a lease administration team of about 11.
baseline.notes: About 1,000 contracts mature each month. Notices and month-to-month renewal follow the contract's end-of-term clause; returns are handed to asset management.

trigger: The contract appears on the lease system's monthly maturity list about 60 to 90 days before its term ends.
end_state: The contract is paid in full and title transfer requested, renewed, rolled to month-to-month rent, handed to asset management for return, or left with collections when the option is not paid.

volume.seasonality: Follows bookings three to five years earlier; little monthly seasonality.

evidence.note: Organisation file demand driver d_maturities: about 70% of booked contracts run to term.

Title, department, layer and loaded cost from the organisation file (2019-2022 wage x 1.35 for benefits, payroll taxes and overhead). FTE is the author's estimate from step times: about 27 minutes of specialist time per maturing contract on average, much more on fair market value contracts.
Title, department, layer and loaded cost from the organisation file (2019-2022 wage x 1.35 for benefits, payroll taxes and overhead). Approves price concessions below the valuation.

Title, department, layer and loaded cost from the organisation file (2019-2022 wage x 1.35 for benefits, payroll taxes and overhead). Values about 140 fair market value contracts a month; this work is also counted in the organisation file's valuation process volume.
Title, department, layer and loaded cost from the organisation file (2019-2022 wage x 1.35 for benefits, payroll taxes and overhead). Logs elections phoned or emailed in by customers.

systems.name: Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Document imaging and contract file store
Contact centre telephony and shared mailboxes
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)
Online auction and equipment listing platforms
General ledger and accounts payable (mid-market ERP)

steps.name: List contracts reaching end of term
steps.description: The lease system's monthly maturity report lists every contract whose term ends in roughly the next 60 to 90 days, with the purchase option type, residual, balance owing, delinquency status and customer contact, and drops it into the lease administration work list.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Lessors flag accounts months ahead and send notices 60 to 180 days before expiry; the monthly batch is an author estimate.

steps.name: Screen the maturing contract
steps.description: A lease administration specialist works down the maturity list, opening each contract image where the lease system field is unclear to confirm the purchase option ($1 or $10, a fixed percentage, an obligation to buy at a stated residual, or fair market value), and checks arrears, collections or legal status, co-terminating schedules and the province for sales tax on the option.

error.defect_description: Option type misread, for example a fair market value contract treated as a $1 buyout so title passes without collecting the value.

next.condition: nominal or fixed purchase option, account current
fair market value option or large residual

evidence.note: Option mix (about 60% nominal, 21% fixed percentage or stated residual, 14% fair market value) and the 5% in arrears are author estimates for a Canadian small-ticket lessor.

steps.name: Place a title hold and alert collections
steps.description: For a contract in arrears the specialist sets a title hold flag in the lease system so no bill of sale is issued until the account is paid in full, and emails the collector working the account with the maturity date and the purchase option amount.

error.defect_description: Hold not set and title released on an unpaid account.

control.basis: Title released only when the contract is paid in full

evidence.note: Author estimate of common practice.

steps.name: Send the purchase option notice
steps.description: The specialist reviews the lease system's mail-merge batch of end-of-term letters for nominal and fixed-option contracts, corrects addresses and amounts that look wrong and releases the letters by mail or email. Each letter states the purchase amount plus taxes, that it will be billed with the final payment, and how to ask about renewal or return where the contract allows it.

error.defect_description: Letter goes to an old address or shows the wrong option amount.

control.basis: End-of-term notice policy and the contract's notice provisions

evidence.note: Notices about 60 days or more before expiry are documented; the batch review and minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Request a fair market value
steps.description: For a fair market value contract the specialist sends a valuation request to asset management with the equipment description, serial numbers, age, original cost, booked residual and any hours, mileage or condition notes from the file.

error.defect_description: Wrong equipment details sent, giving a wrong value.

evidence.note: Manual fair market value entry and coordination with remarketing on market values are documented; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Value the equipment for the fair market value option
steps.description: An asset manager prices the equipment from recent auction results, dealer listings and residual tables, adjusts for age and likely condition, and returns a purchase price and a renewal rate to lease administration with a short note on the basis.

error.defect_description: Value set too high (customer returns equipment worth less) or too low (gain given away).

evidence.note: Fair market value as current resale price and remarketing input are documented; minutes and queue time are author estimates.

steps.name: Send the fair market value options notice
steps.description: The specialist writes an individual letter giving the purchase price at fair market value plus taxes, the renewal payment and term, the return instructions and condition standards, and the date by which the customer must elect, and emails or mails it with an election form.

error.defect_description: Wrong price or election date in the letter.

control.basis: End-of-term notice policy and the contract's notice provisions

evidence.note: Option set, election deadlines and return conditions are documented; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Bill the purchase option with the final payment
steps.description: When the maturity date arrives the lease system adds the purchase option amount and its sales tax to the final invoice and the pre-authorised debit for the last payment, with no manual work.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Calendar wait from notice to maturity follows the 60 to 90 day listing in the organisation file; billing the option with the last payment is an author estimate of common practice.

steps.name: Customer pays the final invoice
steps.description: Most customers pay the final invoice and purchase option by the usual pre-authorised debit on the due date; others pay by cheque or EFT after it arrives, and some do not pay because they forgot, dispute the amount or want to return or refinance the equipment instead.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Payment share is an author estimate; about 85% of customers pay by pre-authorised debit per the organisation file.

steps.name: Chase an unpaid purchase option
steps.description: The specialist calls or emails the customer about the unpaid option amount, explains the contract terms, and agrees whether the customer will pay, refinance the residual over a short renewal, return the equipment where the contract allows it, or leave the account with collections.

error.defect_description: Wrong amount quoted to the customer.

next.condition: customer will not pay; account stays in collections

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Customer replies or the deadline passes
steps.description: The customer compares the fair market value price with buying elsewhere, renewing or returning, and sends the election form, emails or phones in, often close to the deadline. Some customers do not reply at all and the deadline passes.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Election deadlines and month-to-month renewal on silence are documented; the 17% no-reply share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Log the customer's election
steps.description: A customer service representative takes the customer's call or reads the emailed form, records the election (buy, renew, return or upgrade) and any request such as a lower price in the lease system and routes it to the lease administration queue.

error.defect_description: Election recorded wrongly, for example renew instead of return.

next.condition: return or upgrade with the dealer

evidence.note: Election shares among fair market value customers (48% buy, 22% renew, 30% return) are author estimates; returns overall stay near the organisation file's 70 returned assets a month.

steps.name: Confirm or negotiate the purchase price
steps.description: The specialist confirms the purchase price with the customer; when the customer pushes back with its own valuation or a competing quote, the specialist checks with the asset manager what lower price is still above expected resale net of return and remarketing costs.

error.defect_description: Price agreed without the taxes, so the invoice surprises the customer.

next.condition: discount requested beyond the specialist's limit

evidence.note: Lease-end specialists quote buyouts and aim to maximise gross profit on purchase options; shares and minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Approve a price below the valuation
steps.description: The lease administration manager reviews the requested discount against the valuation, the cost of collecting and selling the equipment and the customer's history, and approves it or sets a counter-offer.

error.defect_description: Discount approved without checking the residual booked.

control.basis: Delegated authority for residual and purchase price concessions

evidence.note: Author estimate of a common delegated authority design.

steps.name: Invoice the purchase price at maturity
steps.description: The specialist enters the agreed purchase price as a one-time charge with sales tax for the customer's province, set to bill on or after the maturity date, and sends the customer the invoice with payment instructions.

error.defect_description: Wrong tax province or amount on the invoice.

evidence.note: Sales tax on payoffs is documented; billing at maturity is an author estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the renewal or residual financing agreement
steps.description: For a renewal the specialist prices a fixed renewal term (often 12 months) or confirms the original rate as the contract allows, or sets up a short schedule to finance an unpaid residual, prepares the extension agreement and sends it for e-signature.
inputs: logged election or agreed next step

error.defect_description: Renewal term or rate keyed wrong in the agreement.

evidence.note: Preparing extension documents and renewals at the original rate are documented; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Customer signs the renewal
steps.description: The customer reviews the renewal or extension agreement sent by e-signature and signs it, often after a reminder, or lets it sit unsigned past the maturity date.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Issue return instructions
steps.description: The specialist sends the customer return instructions (return location, de-installation and packing, condition standards, documents to include) and opens a return work item for asset management with the equipment list and site contact, so a carrier can be booked and billing stopped once the equipment arrives.

error.defect_description: Incomplete equipment list or site contact, delaying pickup.

evidence.note: Return arrangements, return conditions and coordination of returns are documented; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Book the renewal in the lease system
steps.description: The specialist checks the signed agreement against the terms offered and books the renewal schedule in the lease system (new payment, term, tax, residual), so billing continues on the new terms, and files the signed agreement in the imaging system.

error.defect_description: Renewal booked with the wrong payment or start date.

evidence.note: Lease extensions are maintained in the lease system; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Start month-to-month billing and send a reminder
steps.description: When no election arrives by maturity, the lease system continues billing month to month under the contract's renewal clause; the specialist confirms the contract has rolled, sends a reminder of the options and notes when to follow up.

error.defect_description: Month-to-month rent set at the wrong rate.

control.basis: Contract renewal clause: month-to-month extension at the applicable rent when the lessee neither elects nor returns

evidence.note: Month-to-month extension at the same rent and reminder notices are documented; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Customer responds during month-to-month
steps.description: After a few month-to-month invoices some customers call to buy or return the equipment; others keep paying rent indefinitely because the equipment is still useful.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Confirm the contract is paid in full
steps.description: About ten business days after the final debit, once a disputed business debit can no longer be reclaimed, the specialist checks that all payments, the purchase amount, taxes, late fees and any protection program charges are paid and that no title hold remains.

error.defect_description: A small outstanding balance is missed and written off later.

control.basis: Title released only after the final payment has cleared (business PAD reimbursement window under Payments Canada Rule H1)

evidence.note: The 10-business-day business PAD claim window is stated in Rule H1; using it as a hold before title release and the 7% with a balance owing are author estimates.

steps.name: Close the contract and stop billing
steps.description: The specialist posts the end-of-term purchase in the lease system, which closes the schedule, stops invoices and debits, records the sale and sales tax and marks the asset sold, and closes the record in the insurance tracking database.

error.defect_description: Billing or the protection program fee not stopped.

evidence.note: Sale with sales tax at payoff is documented; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Send the title transfer request
steps.description: The specialist creates the title transfer request with serial numbers, registration numbers and the buyer's name, so the title team issues the bill of sale and discharges the PPSA or RDPRM registration.

error.defect_description: Request not created, so the customer chases its bill of sale and discharge.

control.basis: Provincial PPSA duty to discharge a registration once obligations are performed (for example BC PPSA s.50(4): within 40 days after a written demand)

evidence.note: Discharge duty stated in the BC Act; the request step is an author estimate.

steps.name: Post end-of-term entries to the general ledger
steps.description: The nightly interface posts the end-of-term sale (receivable closed, residual realised, gain or loss, sales tax payable) from the lease system to the general ledger and the sales tax data used for filing.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Nightly interface is an author estimate.

exceptions.name: Contract in arrears at maturity
exceptions.description: A title hold is set and collections alerted; title waits until the account is paid in full.

exceptions.name: Unpaid purchase option
exceptions.description: The final invoice with the option is not paid; the specialist chases, refinances, takes the equipment back or leaves the account with collections.

exceptions.name: Price negotiation on a fair market value purchase
exceptions.description: The customer counters the valuation and the manager approves a lower price or a counter-offer.

exceptions.name: No reply by maturity
exceptions.description: The contract rolls to month-to-month rent and the specialist sends reminders until the customer buys, returns or keeps renting.

exceptions.name: Renewal agreement not signed
exceptions.description: The customer agreed to renew but did not sign, so the contract rolls to month-to-month.

exceptions.name: Balance owing at the paid-in-full check
exceptions.description: Late fees, a returned debit or tax leave a balance and title waits while it is chased.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the maturity list to title request, renewal, return hand-off or month-to-month
benchmarks.population: Maturing contracts at a Canadian small and mid-ticket equipment lessor, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Derived, not measured: listing 60 to 90 days before maturity (organisation file), notices about 60 days ahead (NBC) or 60 to 180 days (Leasing News), then about two weeks after the final debit for the payment to clear and title to be requested; p90 reflects unpaid options and month-to-month holdovers.

benchmarks.unit: days before expiry that lessors send end-of-term notices

evidence.note: 60 days at NBC; 60, 90 and 180 days in lessor self-reports.
Author estimate driven by the option mix; no published Canadian figure was found. Returns match the organisation file's 50 to 95 off-lease returns a month.
Rule H1 reimbursement provisions.

pain_points.description: Option types sit in contract images and are not always reliable in the lease system, so every maturing contract is screened by hand.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: Fair market value contracts wait days for a valuation and then for the customer, and prices are negotiated case by case.

evidence.note: Valuation and buyout quoting duties are documented; delays are an author view.

pain_points.description: Customers who miss the election deadline roll to month-to-month rent, which brings complaints and reminder work, while others keep paying for years.

evidence.note: Evergreen renewal practices and disputes over charges after term are documented.

pain_points.description: Unpaid purchase options turn into collection work after the contract has technically ended.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: Title cannot be released until the final debit clears, so customers and their banks wait two weeks or more for a bill of sale.

evidence.note: Business PAD claim window; customer chasing is an author view.

sources.title: Equipment financing: End or cancellation of a lease
sources.supports: A Canadian bank lessor sends a letter about 60 days before the lease expires setting out the options: buy at fair market value or the stated purchase option, keep leasing at the original rate, return the equipment (customer calls to arrange the return) or trade up subject to credit.

sources.title: Equipment financing: Lease contract conditions
sources.supports: Fair market value is the price the lessor can sell the equipment for in current market conditions; the lessor owns the equipment until the buyout.

sources.title: Companies who notify lessee in advance of lease expiration
sources.supports: Self-reported lessor practices: written notices at 60, 90 or 180 days before expiry, follow-ups at 90, 60 and 30 days; some lessors renew month to month when the lessee neither buys nor returns, one at 50% of the payment; others stop billing at term end; one flags accounts 3 to 6 months ahead.

sources.title: End of Term Notice sample clauses
sources.supports: Equipment lease clause: the lessee must give at least 90 days' notice of its election to buy, return or extend; without notice or return the schedule extends month to month at the applicable rent; notice is irrevocable.

sources.title: Evaluating end-of-lease options
sources.supports: End-of-lease choices are return (meeting the lessor's return conditions), renew (possibly renegotiating term and payment) or purchase at a set price.

sources.title: Lease End Specialist (job posting)
sources.supports: Lease-end duties: explain options, review contract terms, quote buyouts and extension payments, prepare extension documents, coordinate returns and inspection reports, work with remarketing on market values.

sources.title: LeasePak reference guide: Payoff Quote [U0213]
sources.supports: Residual-based payoffs and termination quotes need a manually entered fair market value; sales tax applies to payoffs, not terminations.

sources.title: LeasePak reference guide: Termination [U0103]
sources.supports: Termination returns equipment to the lessor: month-to-month leases can be terminated, the asset goes to inventory at the lower of fair market value and net book value, wear and tear and excess use charges are added, and automatic lease extensions must be updated.

sources.title: Personal Property Security Act [RSBC 1996] chapter 359
sources.supports: Section 50(4): a registration must be discharged not later than 40 days after a written demand once obligations are performed; the Act covers leases for a term of more than one year.

sources.title: Rule H1: Pre-authorized debits (PADs)
sources.supports: A payor may claim reimbursement of a disputed business PAD up to 10 business days after the debit (90 calendar days for a personal PAD); an NSF PAD may be re-presented once, within 30 calendar days, for the same amount.

sources.title: Wages: Accounting and related clerks (NOC 14200)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low $18.12, median $25.00, high $37.00 (2023-2024).

assumptions: Purchase option mix for this small-ticket book: about 60% nominal ($1 or $10), 21% fixed percentage or stated residual, 14% fair market value, plus 5% in arrears at maturity; all author estimates.
The case clock starts when the contract appears on the maturity list, so most elapsed time is the calendar wait to the maturity date (step s08) and is not a queue.
Valuations (s06) are done by asset managers and are the same work the organisation file counts in value-equipment-and-set-residuals; a whole-organisation model should count them once.
The asset_valuation link from the valuation process starts no case, so its share is 0; it arrives at step s06.
Returns end this workflow when the return instruction reaches asset management; transport, inspection, wear charges and the billing stop belong to recover-off-lease-equipment.
Upgrades through the dealer are treated as returns (dealer takes the old equipment) or purchases (dealer pays the option); they are not modelled separately.

Organisation file issue: lease administration has 10 specialists. This workflow needs about 3.5 FTE and payouts about 3.5 FTE, leaving about 3 FTE for 1,250 title transfers a month plus restructures and assumptions, which looks thin.
External steps carry no touch time; the customer's effort sits inside the waits.
